issue: Must an indictment charging a continuing criminal enterprise under 21 U.S.C. § 848 identify the three predicate narcotics violations by statutory reference, or must courts apply a facts-and-circumstances test to decide whether the indictment is sufficient?

sides.position: An indictment charging a CCE offense is sufficient when it specifies the predicate violations by reference to statutory sections, or when other counts describe the predicate narcotics violations; no facts-and-circumstances test is needed.
cases: United States v. Montague, 67 F.4th 520 (2d Cir. 2023)

sides.position: Whether an indictment charging a CCE offense is sufficient is judged under a facts-and-circumstances test rather than by a fixed pleading rule.
cases: United States v. Bansal, 663 F.3d 634 (3d Cir. 2011)

this_court: The Second Circuit follows the Flaharty approach and holds the Montague indictment sufficient. It does not adopt the Third Circuit's facts-and-circumstances test, and it says any split emerged from Bansal rather than from its own decision.
quote: The dissent claims that our decision creates a circuit split with the Third Circuit's decision in Bansal.
cite: United States v. Montague, 67 F.4th 520 (2d Cir. 2023)
